data.title: Ribosomal protein S6 phosphorylation is a determinant of cell size and glucose homeostasis
data.authors: Ruvinsky I; Sharon N; Lerer T; Cohen H; Stolovich-Rain M; Nir T; Dor Y; Zisman P; Meyuhas O

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Knock-in mice with all five rpS6 phosphorylation sites mutated to alanine (rpS6P-/-); embryonic fibroblasts; pancreatic beta-cells; glucose tolerance tests
data.finding: The authors made knock-in mice in which all five phosphorylatable serines of ribosomal protein S6 were replaced by alanine, so rpS6 could not be phosphorylated. Contrary to the then widely accepted model, translational control of 5'TOP mRNAs was unaffected. Fibroblasts from these mice made protein faster and divided faster, yet were smaller than wild-type cells, and rapamycin did not shrink them further, which points to rpS6 phosphorylation as a downstream effector of mTOR in cell-size control. Adult mutant mice also had smaller pancreatic beta-cells, less pancreatic insulin, low blood insulin and impaired glucose tolerance. Boundary: Mouse knock-in and mouse cells. Separates rpS6 phosphorylation from 5'TOP control in these systems; not tested in people. Drafted from the abstract only.
data.abstract_excerpt: The regulated phosphorylation of ribosomal protein (rp) S6 has attracted much attention since its discovery in 1974, yet its physiological role has remained obscure. To directly address this issue, we have established viable and fertile knock-in mice, whose rpS6 contains alanine substitutions at all five phosphorylatable serine residues (rpS6(P-/-)). Here we show that contrary to the widely accepted model, this mutation does not affect the translational control of TOP mRNAs.

extracted_findings.target: 5'TOP translation; protein synthesis; cell size; beta-cell size; glucose tolerance
extracted_findings.effect: Loss of rpS6 phosphorylation reduces cell and beta-cell size and impairs glucose tolerance without affecting 5'TOP translation
